instructions: Pour the 6 cups broth into a large pot, cover it and bring it to a boil over high.
Meanwhile, pull the stems off the shiitake and slice the caps thin. Drain the bamboo shoots and cut them into thin strips.
Cut the tofu into strips about 1/4 inch thick and 2 inches long.
Beat the 2 eggs in a small bowl. Thinly slice 2 of the green onions. In a cup, stir the 1/4 cup cornstarch with 3 tbsp water until there are no lumps.
When the broth boils, stir in the 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp sugar, 3/4 tsp of the white pepper, 1 1/2 tsp dark soy sauce, 2 tsp soy sauce and the 1 tsp sesame oil.
Add the mushrooms and bamboo shoots and simmer for 3 minutes, until the mushrooms are soft.
Slide in the tofu, pour in the 1/4 cup vinegar and stir gently. Bring it back to a simmer.

Give the cornstarch mix another stir. Stir the soup in a slow circle and pour the cornstarch in a thin stream as you go. Keep stirring for about 1 minute, until the soup is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Keep the soup at a gentle bubble and keep stirring slowly with one hand. With the other, drizzle in the eggs in a thin stream. They'll set into ribbons in a few seconds. Turn off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a splash more of the vinegar.
Ladle it into bowls and scatter the green onions on top. Serve with the rest of the white pepper on the side.
method_notes: Both season chicken stock with soy, dark soy, sugar, white pepper and sesame oil, simmer mushrooms, bamboo shoots and tofu in it, sour it with plain white vinegar, thicken it with a cornstarch slurry and finish with egg ribbons and green onion. The Woks of Life adds julienned pork, spiced dry tofu, lily flowers and dried wood ear and shiitake that soak for 1 to 2 hours; RecipeTin Eats poaches chicken breast in the stock and allows fresh shiitake. This one follows The Woks of Life's seasoning scaled to 4, leaves out the meat for more tofu, and uses fresh shiitake and skips the dried lily flowers and wood ear to keep it to twenty minutes.
